run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: I could not tie request REQ-EU-8K4M2 to any service: the Elasticsearch target contains only synthetic app-185-geo-* log indices whose 162 in-window documents are uniformly INFO / 150 ms, phrase searches for the request ID returned nothing, and both the Prometheus and Jaeger query endpoints answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every attempt in this Run. What the evidence does show is that all 22 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready, that every otel-demo container was restarted together at 2026-11-21T04:23:47Z-04:24:34Z after a previous termination with exit code 255 (a node/runtime-scale event, not an app rollout), and that the demo's fault-injection flags in ConfigMap flagd-config are all set to defaultVariant off at query time. Sampled application logs for checkout, product-catalog, payment, ad, cart and recommendation show normal activity without error lines. Consequently no service can be named as affected on its own evidence, and no root cause is identified.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target contains 1620 matched indices, and the name prefixes returned for pattern app-185-* are all of the form app-185-geo-<region>-<service> (6 regions ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, eu-west, us-east, us-west x 27 services such as checkout, cart, catalog, payments).

The mapping of index app-185-geo-eu-west-web-2024.01.01 contains only @timestamp (date), level, message, region, response_time_ms (long) and service; there is no request-id, trace-id, status-code or error field.

A match_all search over index pattern * inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T08:56:11Z-2026-11-21T08:56:11Z matched 162 documents, bucketed as 27 services in each of the 6 regions, with avg and max response_time_ms equal to 150 in every region.
The level terms aggregation over the same 162 in-window documents returned only the INFO bucket (doc_count 162); no ERROR or WARN bucket was returned.

The 10 documents returned by the log search were level INFO with message "Request completed successfully" and response_time_ms 150, for example from app-185-geo-eu-central-analytics-2024.01.10, app-185-geo-eu-central-checkout-2024.01.10 and app-185-geo-eu-central-cart-2024.01.10 at @timestamp 2026-11-21T08:54:00Z.

All 22 pods in namespace otel-demo were in phase Running with their container ready=true at query time (e.g. frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw, checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, prometheus-9bc78b5f7-c9wx8, jaeger-698d849b7b-sjz9c).

Every otel-demo container was restarted between 2026-11-21T04:23:47Z and 2026-11-21T04:24:34Z; 20 pods record a previous termination with exit code 255 (including jaeger and prometheus-server), kube-state-metrics with exit code 1 and prometheus-readonly-proxy with exit code 1 (restartCount 3).

No ReplicaSet in namespace otel-demo was created after 2026-11-20T16:33:37Z, and the images are unchanged; otel-collector and prometheus each keep an older 0-replica ReplicaSet (otel-collector-845f9747bd, prometheus-547d4cbb8) with the same image as the active one.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo defines fault flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and at query time every one of them has defaultVariant "off".

The Prometheus ConfigMap contains an alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh that computes the 5-minute error ratio of checkout server spans named *CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and fires above 0.5; this is configuration only and does not show that the alert fired.

The sampled checkout logs between 2026-11-21T08:47:16Z and 08:55:52Z show repeated successful sequences "[PlaceOrder] user_id=...", "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and "order confirmation email sent to ..." with severity info.
The product-catalog pod logged "Reloading Product Catalog..." and "Loaded 10 products" every 10 seconds through 2026-11-21T08:56:08Z at level=info.
The Prometheus pod logs show it is receiving OTLP metric writes, logging "Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars" warnings with num_dropped values each minute up to 2026-11-21T08:55:49Z.
Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False.

The only Kubernetes events inside the window were 3 Warning events with reason FailedToCreateEndpoint for Endpoints clickhouse (namespace app-222), mysql (app-218) and postgres (app-217) between 08:28:31Z and 08:44:22Z; no event involved an otel-demo object.

The 04:23 restart cannot be attributed to an application failure: no Evicted, OOMKilled or Unhealthy event was returned for otel-demo, the previous termination reason is recorded as "Unknown" with exit 255 (not OOMKilled), and all pods are Ready with no node memory/disk/PID pressure.

Rejected: that the 04:23 container restarts were a deployment rollout with a changed pod template. No ReplicaSet was created after 2026-11-20T16:33:37Z, pod template images are unchanged, and the oldest/active ReplicaSets share the same image digests.

The simultaneous termination and restart of every otel-demo container at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z-04:24:34Z with exit code 255 is most consistent with a node/container-runtime restart of opspilot-m1-control-plane; what triggered it is not observable in the collected data.

The Prometheus/Jaeger query outage seen by the tools may be related to the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx container, which had restartCount 3 with a previous exit code 1 at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z and whose nginx.conf is mounted from a Secret that cannot be read; this is unverified.

A latency/fault flag of the demo (for example imageSlowLoad, paymentFailure or adHighCpu) could produce the reported slow response with an error page, but the current flagd-config shows every flag off and no span or error metric could be read, so this remains unsupported for the incident time.

gaps: No trace of request REQ-EU-8K4M2 could be obtained: every traces_search, traces_search_by_tags, traces_query_trace_by_id, traces_list_services and traces_list_operations call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (attempts from 2026-11-21T08:56:14Z to 08:59:38Z), so the request's spans, service and error tags are unknown.

No Prometheus series could be read: get_metric_names, get_series, get_label_values, get_metric_metadata, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so latency, error-rate, rpc_* and traces_span_metrics_calls_total values and alert states for the window are unknown, including whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh fired.

Phrase searches of Elasticsearch for "REQ-EU-8K4M2", "REQ-EU" and "8K4M2" over index pattern * inside the authorized window returned no documents (0 hits each), so the request ID is not locatable in the log store that is exposed here; documents older than the window or in another store could not be searched.

The frontend (frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw), frontend-proxy (frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn), load-generator and jaeger pods returned zero log lines for the window, so the customer-facing request path and Jaeger's own logs could not be inspected.
The nginx configuration of prometheus-readonly-proxy and the Prometheus web config are mounted from Secrets that cannot be read, so the proxy's upstream/auth correctness could not be verified.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change record (who changed flagd flags, ConfigMaps or the proxy configuration, and when) can be consulted.
No evidence ties the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z node-wide container restart to the customer complaint, and its trigger is unknown.
next_steps: Obtain the exact timestamp of the customer's failed request from the error page and re-query logs/traces around that instant.
Once Jaeger is reachable, search spans tagged with the request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 (or the trace ID shown on the error page) and inspect the error span's service, operation and parent references.

Once Prometheus read access through prometheus-readonly-proxy is restored, query traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name/status_code and the checkout PlaceOrder error ratio plus rpc_client_duration_milliseconds for the window to identify the slow dependency.
Review the Secret-backed nginx.conf of prometheus-readonly-proxy and the Prometheus web config, and verify the read-only query path used by the tooling.
Consult change history (not integrated here) for flagd-config, ConfigMaps and Secret changes made at or before 2026-11-21T04:23Z and during the customer incident window.

receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        credentials_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        type: Bearer
    max_alerts: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
